All coolers are equipment.

Some equipment are mobiles.

questions.question: Which two signs and which two numbers should be interchanged in the following equation to make it correct? 17 - 8 + 2 × 6 ÷ 3 = 3
questions.solution:
Given equation:

17 - 8 + 2 × 6 ÷ 3 = 3

BODMAS Rule:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/aa4b32c5c2a037a20e4d4661359c3196b0f71063271e5df111ac933b7666f423.png] 

1) × and +; 17 and 8

17 - 8 + 2 × 6 ÷ 3 = 3

Interchanging and using BODMAS rule:

8 - 17 + 2 ÷ 6 × 3 

8 - 17 + 0.33 × 3

8 - 17 + 1

9 - 17

- 8 ≠ 3

2) × and -; 8 and 6

17 - 8 + 2 × 6 ÷ 3 = 3

Interchanging and using BODMAS rule:

17 × 6 + 2 - 8 ÷ 3 

17 × 6 + 2 - 2.67

102 + 2 - 2.67

104 - 2.67

101.33 ≠ 3

**3) + and ×, 2 and 8**

**17 - 8 + 2 × 6 ÷ 3 = 3**

**Interchanging and using BODMAS rule:**

**17 - 2 × 8 + 6 ÷ 3 **

**17 - 2 × 8 + 2**

**17 - 16 + 2**

**19 - 16**

**3 = 3**

4) - and +, 6 and 3

17 - 8 + 2 × 6 ÷ 3 = 3

Interchanging and using BODMAS rule:

17 + 8 - 2 × 3 ÷ 6

17 + 8 - 2 × 0.5

17 + 8 - 1

25 - 1

24 ≠ 3

Hence, the correct answer is **"**+ and ×, 2 and 8**"**.

questions.question: Before 4 years, the age of A was twice the age of B. After 6 years, the age of C will be twice the age of A. The current age of A is 10 years more than that of B. What is the current age of C?
questions.solution:
Given,

The current age of A is 10 years more than that of B.

A = B + 10

B = A - 10

Let the current age of A be x.

⇒ Current age of B = x - 10

Given,

Before 4 years, the age of A was twice the age of B.

A - 4 = 2 (B - 4)

x - 4 = 2(x - 10 - 4)

x - 4 = 2(x - 14)

x - 4 = 2x - 28

2x - x = 28 - 4

x = 24

So, the present age of A = 24

Given, 

After 6 years, the age of C will be twice the age of A.

Let the present age of C be C.

C + 6 = 2(A + 6)

C + 6 = 2 (24 + 6)

C + 6 = 2(30)

C + 6 = 60

C = 60 - 6

C = 54

So, the present age of C is 54.

Hence, the correct answer is **"54"**.

questions.question:
Which two numbers should be interchanged in the following equation to make it correct?

45 ÷ 5 + 15 × 6 - 14 = 78
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/884eed145919fc7a8edee924e13c89ab88eb6bd532da0c19a99a1493b7c609f7.png] 

The logic follows here is :

Given equation → 45 ÷ 5 + 15 × 6 - 14 = 78

**(I). 45 ÷ 5 + 15 × 6 - 14 = 78**

**Interchanging (14 and 15) and applying BODMAS rule,**

**45 ÷ 5 + 14 × 6 - 15 = 78**

**9 + 14 × 6 - 15 = 78**

**9 + 84 - 15 = 78**

**93 - 15 = 78**

**78 = 78.**

**LHS = RHS.**

(II). 45 ÷ 5 + 15 × 6 - 14 = 78

Interchanging **(5 and 15)** and applying **BODMAS** rule,

45 ÷ 15 + 5 × 6 - 14 = 78

3 + 5 × 6 - 14 = 78

3 + 30 - 14 = 78

33 - 14 = 78

19 ≠ 78.

LHS ≠ RHS.

(III). 45 ÷ 5 + 15 × 6 - 14 = 78

Interchanging (5 and 6) and applying BODMAS rule,

45 ÷ 6 + 15 × 5 - 14 = 78

7.5 + 15 × 5 - 14 = 78

7.5 + 75 -14 = 78

82.5 - 14 = 78

68.5 ≠ 78.

LHS ≠ RHS.

(IV). 45 ÷ 5 + 15 × 6 - 14 = 78

Interchanging (45 and 15) and applying BODMAS rule,

15 ÷ 5 + 45 × 6 - 14 = 78

3 + 45 × 6 - 14 = 78

3 + 270 -14 = 78

273 - 14 = 78

259 ≠ 78.

LHS ≠ RHS.

Hence, the correct answer is **"**14 and 15".

questions.question: Neerav is facing southeast. He then turns 135° clockwise. After that he turns 90° anticlockwise. Now he turns 225° clockwise. Which direction is he facing now?
questions.solution:
According to the given information :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3dd74d7c93016c9dd781243d6b578d89605242d0011fe07911a633cc4eccf5da.png] 

Finally, Neerav is facing **North-East.**

Hence, the correct answer is **"Northeast".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

The initial direction is Southeast.

Consider clockwise as (+) and anti-clockwise as (-).

The series of turns is as follows :** **

135∘ clockwise → 90∘ anti-clockwise → 225∘ clockwise

**(+ 135∘) + (- 90∘) + (+ 225∘) = 135∘ - 90∘ + 225∘ = 270∘ **

The value is positive, means it is clockwise.

270∘ clockwise from Southeast will be** Northeast.**

**OR**

**(360∘ - 270∘) = 90∘ anti-clockwise.**

90∘ anti-clockwise from Southeast will be** Northeast.** 

Hence, the correct answer is "Northeast".

questions.question: Maheep starts walking from his office and walks 120 m towards south. Then he turns left and walks a certain distance A m. Then turns right and walks 80 m. Then he turns left and walks another certain distance B m. He there by reaches his home. If the shortest distance between his office and home is 290 m, then what is the sum of the distances A and B that Maheep covered/walked?
questions.solution:
According to the given information :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/df7794fd41ef757611c5c58811f2ab39260e6debe60bb0d89bad7e32f2229a6d.png] 

Shortest distance between office and home = OP = 290 m.

OQ = 120 + 80 = 200 m.

PQ = A + B.

In right angled ΔOPQ, by Pythagoras Theorem :

(OP)² = (OQ)² + (PQ)²

290² = 200² + (A + B)²

84100 = 40000 + (A + B)2

84100 - 40000 = (A + B)2

44100 = (A + B)2

(A + B) = √44100

**(A + B) = 210.** 

Hence, the correct answer is **"210 m".**

questions.question: Among six commodities P, Q, R, S, T and U, the price of Q is 1.5 times that of T. The price of U is four times that of P. The price of S is equal to the price of R. The price of P is 3.5 times that of R. The price of T is twice the price of R. The price of P is Rs. 70. What is the price of Q?
questions.solution:
Given that :

Price of P = Rs. 70

Price of U is four times that of P

U = 4P = 4 × 70 = Rs. 280

Price of P is 3.5 times that of R

P = 3.5R

R = P/3.5

R = 70/3.5 = Rs. 20

Price of R = Price of S

Price of T is twice the price of R

T = 2R

T = 2 × 20 = Rs. 40

**Price of Q is 1.5 times that of T**

**Q = 1.5T = 1.5 × 40 = Rs. 60.**

Hence, the correct answer is **"Rs. 60".**

questions.question: Six subjects Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Ecology, Hindi and English are taught from Monday to Saturday. Each day, one subject is taught. Hindi is taught just after Ecology and just before English. Biology is taught after English. Physics and Ecology are taught on Tuesday and Wednesday respectively. Which subject is taught on Monday?
questions.solution:

questions.question: In a class of 170 students, 155 students take part in either one or more than one class of either guitar, drum or violin. A total of 21 students take part in any two of the classes. 54 students take part only in drum classes, whereas 43 students take part in violin class only. Only 5 students take part in all the three classes. How many students take part only in guitar classes?
questions.solution:
There is a total of 170 students in a class.

Out of which 155 students participate in one or more of the three classes: Guitar, Drum, and Violin.

170 - 155 = 15 students who didn't participate in any of the activities.

54 students participate in the Drum class only.

43 students participate in Violin class only.

5 students participate in all three classes.

Total 21 students participate in any and only two of three classes.

Using the above information and drawing the Venn diagram we get.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d7e991471d1e999aaecc352853d4662b6f39d792c080c20665f913c14a8766b7.png] 

As the given** total of 21 students participates in any and only two of three classes.**

**A + B + C = 21**

54 + 5 + 43 + X + **(A + B + C)** = 155

102 + 21 + X = 155

**X = 155 - 123**

**X = 32.**

Hence, the correct answer is **"32".**
